sources.name: U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission recalls
sources.terms: U.S. federal government work, public domain; API documented for public use.

sources.name: SaferProducts.gov incident reports (OData)
sources.access_method: OData API with a free application key
sources.why_not: needs an API key (SAFERPRODUCTS_API_KEY) that is not set up
sources.terms: Public incident reports; key registration required. Reports are consumer allegations, not findings.

sources.name: OECD GlobalRecalls portal (regulators' notices, incl. ACCC, CAA, KATS, CPSO, BSMI, ASEAN)
sources.terms: (c) OECD, all rights reserved (oecd.org/termsandconditions). SafeShelf keeps metadata, short excerpts and the link; no bulk republication. Singapore and ASEAN feeds stopped arriving in 2022; New Zealand and India are not in it.

sources.name: ACCC Product Safety Australia recalls (RSS)
sources.why_not: the site refuses automated requests (checked 2026-10-16); a person needs to look
sources.terms: Official public feed. From SafeShelf's network the site answers 403 (Akamai) to plain HTTP and headless browsers; Australian notices come through OECD GlobalRecalls until the feed answers.

sources.name: Consumer Affairs Agency recall information site (Japan)
sources.access_method: Public HTML pages (new-registrations list and notice detail pages); plain HTTP
sources.terms: Public Data License 1.0 (PDL1.0), per recall.caa.go.jp/about: reuse allowed with the source credited, and edits marked as edits. Japanese text is kept as published.

sources.name: NITE product accident information (Japan)
sources.access_method: Site reachable by plain HTTP; no documented query interface found yet
sources.why_not: access method and terms not verified yet, so SafeShelf does not query it
sources.terms: Not yet reviewed for automated querying.

sources.name: METI product safety recall notices (Japan)
sources.why_not: the site refuses automated requests (checked 2026-10-16); a person needs to look
sources.terms: Answers 403 to automated requests from SafeShelf's network. CAA's site links METI's notices, so they are reached through jp_caa.

sources.name: Consumer Product Safety Office recalls and alerts (Singapore)
sources.why_not: the site refuses automated requests (checked 2026-10-16); a person needs to look
sources.terms: Answers 403 to plain HTTP and headless browsers from SafeShelf's network. Older CPSO notices (to 2022) come through OECD GlobalRecalls.

sources.name: SAFETY Mark registered controlled goods (Singapore)
sources.access_method: Public registry search; no documented machine interface found
sources.why_not: access method and terms not verified yet, so SafeShelf does not query it
sources.terms: Not yet reviewed. A missing SAFETY Mark only matters for the 33 controlled goods categories.

sources.name: EU Safety Gate alerts
sources.access_method: JavaScript portal; works in a headless browser (Research Agent). No permitted public JSON endpoint confirmed.
sources.why_not: only searchable in a browser, and the Research Agent is not configured here
sources.terms: Official public portal. Searched only through the read-only Research Agent.

sources.name: Product Safety New Zealand recalls
sources.access_method: HTML site, searched by the Research Agent
sources.why_not: only searchable in a browser, and the Research Agent is not configured here
sources.terms: Official public site; answers plain HTTP. Not in OECD GlobalRecalls.

sources.name: India CCPA recall orders, safety notices and BIS raids (Press Information Bureau releases)
sources.access_method: Official PIB press releases, fetched by plain HTTP and stored (data/load_india_notices.py); answered from the stored copy
sources.terms: Government of India press releases, published for public use with credit. India has no public recall database.

sources.name: BIS product certification (CRS / ISI licence) verification
sources.access_method: Public lookup on bis.gov.in for people; no automation API
sources.why_not: no automated access exists; a person can check it by hand
sources.terms: Public lookup does not imply automated access. SafeShelf reports "not verified" and gives the shopper the lookup link; it never calls a mark fake because it could not check it.

sources.name: Manufacturer-authorised recall feeds
sources.access_method: Feeds a manufacturer authorises (none signed up yet)
sources.why_not: no automated access exists; a person can check it by hand

sources.name: SafeShelf's stored copy of official notices (CPSC, ACCC, CAA, KATS, CPSO, BSMI, ASEAN, CCPA, BIS)
sources.access_method: Postgres recalls table, loaded by data/load_*.py from the official sources above
sources.terms: Each row keeps its regulator's link and terms.

note: Health since this server started. A source that is not enabled is reported in every answer as 'not supported' or 'source unavailable', never as 'no recall'.
